predictions.text: Bad runs happen, especially in 88 degree weather. You were able to finish eight so you'll be able to finish 10, even if it's going to suck. But the long run jumping four miles in two weeks to 10 miles 10 weeks before the race is a bit unusual -- I'd guess this is an intermediate or advanced plan -- and if this is your first half marathon I'd suggest switching plans if only because of injury risk. Your training plan shouldn't be punishing.

A lot of Very Serious Runners don’t seem to understand something about vests: they’re fashionable to a lot of people. Yes, most people don’t NEED a vest at the local 5K, but they do offer some storage and people simply like how they look. Did I NEED an arm sleeve like Allen Iverson when I was in 6th grade, getting 5 minutes per game off the bench? Nope. But it made me feel cool. Same thing goes for vests. People like how they look wearing a vest and I say more power to them.

Couple things: hydration vests - advantageous to the bladders de to easier to clean; clings tight to body so its barely noticeable when running; storing water and fuel. Practical benefits for longer / hotter efforts. I use mi e as a hiking daypack too which is nice fuel: back then, runners just ran without ingesting much calories. There is now a shift to high carbs for running (especially harder/longer efforts) due to new research regarding the performance/recovery benefits of carbs. shoes: SO many more shoe options. Carbon plates, stability shoes, shoes for fast workouts, shoes for recovery runs, shoes for long runs, daily trainers… too many. It’s just consumerism. Companies releasing a new version of the show every year with slight changes and sometimes those changes are worse than the prior iteration.. nose strips: some runners wear nose strips which open up your nostril and allow you to get more oxygen intake through your nose. It’s a trendy gimmick.

I wear a vest for long runs, where keeping myself supplied with water is an issue (I used to stop at a store and buy water on every long run). For normal runs I wear a flip belt with my phone, usually bring a small bottle of water in the flip belt but rarely drink from it if my run is less than an hour.

I love love love my vest. I only run 3-5 miles at a time. But it is so much better than a belt, in my opinion. I felt like I was constantly adjusting my belts, stuffing phones, keys, water bottles into it. Vest just has more space - ran colder weather the other day and ended up taking my gloves off and had a pocket to stuff them in. I felt silly at first, Somer people saying "you dont need anything if youre only running a few miles" but screw it, I say wear whatever youre comfortable with.
